result.topic_en: Calculations on the first variation of arc length (geodesics) for a quadratic line element $ds^2=\sum a_{i,k}dx_i dx_k$, introducing a characteristic function $\sigma=\tfrac12\sum a^0 x'^0 x'^0 s^2$ and expressing the initial and final direction components through its partial derivatives.
result.transcription:
$ds^2=\sum a_{i,k}dx_i d_k$
$\sum a_{i,k}x_i x_k = const = \sum a^0_{i,k}x^0_i x^0_k$
$\delta s=\delta\int\sqrt{\sum a_{i,k}dx_i d_k}=\int\left(\frac{\sum a_{i,k}dx_i\delta dx_k}{ds\,[?]}+\frac{\tfrac12\sum\frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_{i'}}dx_i dx_k\delta x_{i'}}{ds}\right)=\left(\sum a_{i,k}p_i\delta x_k\right)_0+\int\left(-\frac{d\sum a_{i,k}dx_i}{ds}+\frac{\tfrac12\sum\frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_{i'}}dx_i dx_k}{ds}\right)\delta x_{i'}$
$\delta s=\sum a_{i,k}p_i\delta x_k-\sum a^0_{i,k}p^0_i\delta x^0_k+\int\left(-d\sum a_{i,k}p_i+\tfrac12\sum\frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_{i'}}p_i p_k\right)dx_{i'}$
$=\delta[-(\sqrt{\sum a^0_{i,k}p^0_i p^0_k}\,ds)-]=\delta\int\sqrt{\sum a_{i,k}dx_i dx_k}=\sum a_{i,k}p_i\delta x_k-\sum a^0_{i,k}p_i\delta x^0_k$
$s=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\sum a^0_{i,i'}x'^0_i x'^0_{i'}}}\int\sqrt{\sum a_{i,i'}dx_i dx_{i'}}$
$\delta\left(\sqrt{\sum a^0_{i,i'}x'^0_i x'^0_{i'}}\,s\right)=\delta\int\sqrt{\sum a_{i,i'}dx_i dx_{i'}}=\frac{\sum a_{i,i'}dx_i\delta x_{i'}-\sum a^0_{i,i'}dx^0_i\delta x^0_{i'}}{\sqrt{\sum a^0_{i,i'}dx'^0_i x'^0_{i'}}}$
$=\sum\delta x^0\delta x'^0\,\partial s\,[?]$
$\tfrac12\sum a^0_{i,i'}x'^0_i x'^0_{i'}s^2=\sigma$
$\sqrt{\sum a^0_{i,i'}x'^0_i x'^0_{i'}}\;s\,\delta s\,\sqrt{\sum a^0_{i,i'}x'^0_i x'^0_{i'}}=\delta\sigma=s\sum a_{i,i'}x'_i\delta x_{i'}-s\sum a^0_{i,i'}x'^0_i\delta x^0_{i'}$
$\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x_i}=s\sum a_{i,i'}x'_{i'}$ \quad $s x'_i=\sum\alpha_{i,i'}\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x_{i'}}$
$\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x^0_i}=-s\sum a^0_{i,i'}x'^0_{i'}$ \quad $s x'^0_i=-\sum\alpha^0_{i,i'}\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x^0_{i'}}$
$\sum_{i'}\alpha_{i,i'}a_{i,i'}=1;\ \sum\alpha_{i,i''}a_{i,i'}=0$
$s^2\sum a_{i,i'}x'_i x'_{i'}=\sum\alpha_{i,i'}\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x_{i'}}\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x_i}=2\sigma$
[-$x$-] $\sigma_1=(x_1\ldots x_n,a_1,\ldots a_n)$
$\frac{\partial\sigma_1}{\partial x_i}=(x_1\ldots x_n,a_1,\ldots a_n)$
$a_i=(x_1\ldots x_n,\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x_1},\ldots\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x_n})$
$x'_i=(x_1\ldots x_n,\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x_1},\ldots\frac{\partial\sigma}{\partial x_n})$

$\sum a_{i,i'}x'_i x'_{i'}=1$
$\sum da_{i,i'}x'_i x'_{i'}+2\sum a_{i,i'}x'_i dx'_{i'}=0$
$x_1=(x^0_1\ldots x'^0_1\ldots s)$
$x_n=\ldots$
$x'_1=(x^0_1\ldots x'^0_1\ldots s)$
$x'_n=(\ldots)$
$x'_1=(x_1\ldots x_n,x^0_1\ldots x^0_n,s)$
$x'_n=(x_1,\ldots x_n,x^0_1\ldots x^0_n,s)$
$x'^0_1=(x_1,\ldots x_n,x^0_1\ldots x^0_n,s)$
$x'^0_n=\ldots$
$dx_1=dx^0\ldots dx'^0\ldots ds$

methods.what: First variation of arc length of a Riemannian line element, giving boundary terms plus the geodesic (Euler–Lagrange) equations
methods.quote: $\delta s=\sum a_{i,k}p_i\delta x_k-\sum a^0_{i,k}p^0_i\delta x^0_k+\int\left(-d\sum a_{i,k}p_i+\tfrac12\sum\frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_{i'}}p_i p_k\right)dx_{i'}$

methods.what: Definition of the characteristic function sigma (half squared geodesic distance)
Gradients of sigma give initial and final direction vectors
Inverse metric coefficients alpha defined by reciprocity with a
